- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85+ → 86+), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias after peaks.
- Lags in downward corrections: model takes 2–3 days to recognize falling trends, often underestimating the drop.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum: model assumes trend continues longer than actual mean reversion.
- High variance in forecast error near 70–80 range — model struggles with volatility in mid-range prices.
- Model tends to smooth out sharp drops, underestimating magnitude of declines.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days — adjust downward by 1–2% for early periods.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model often fails to anticipate the next 3–5-day dip.
- Model overreacts to recent spikes — forecasts too high immediately after a peak, then drops too slowly.
